correctness.rationale: Conditional on a sampled box B of independent side lengths, containment of each other box has probability Vol(B)^2; binomial expansion and the exact triangular length moments give the finite sum. The product-length density has coefficient 2^d/(d-1)! at the logarithmic singularity, and Gaussian scaling gives sqrt(pi)/(d-1)! times sqrt(n)(log n)^(d-1). For d=2 the exact density 4[(1+z)log(1/z)-2(1-z)] yields the explicit Euler-constant second term with O(log n) remainder. Any finite family is pierced precisely when its inclusion-minimal subfamily is pierced. The independent standard-library checker passed 255 finite exact/integral assertions; the all-size argument does not depend on them.

originality.rationale: The primary full-text random-box piercing paper studies the optimal hitting-set cardinality, not containment-minimal subfamilies. The original full-text union-of-rectangles calculation treats covered Lebesgue measure, not containment. The box-packing paper treats disjoint packing, but its complete postscript was not retrieved. The separately documented one-dimensional interval result is neither a general-box formula nor a sharp logarithmic dimension law. Targeted published-result searches for random box inclusion minima returned no covering or directly equivalent finding. Residual historical-priority risk is acknowledged; lack of hits is not a uniqueness certificate.

value.rationale: Containment pruning is a lossless reduction of random-box piercing instances, and the surviving cardinality is a natural quantitative preprocessing invariant. A sharp dimension-dependent sqrt(n)(log n)^(d-1) expected size, exact all-n combinatorial expression, and planar second-order coefficient quantify the effect of independent aspect ratios. This is not merely a known union-area or optimal piercing-number estimate. The result is mathematically and algorithmically interpretable without claiming a new piercing optimum.
